newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks mixed amid bank acquisition talk.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks mixed amid bank acquisition talk.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended mixed on Monday, as Banco Comercial Antioqueno (Bancoquia) rose on speculation that Spain's Banco de Santander was interested in buying a stake in the bank.

Bogota's IBB edged up 0.29 percent to 832.76 as 9.9 billion pesos worth of shares changed hands. Medellin's IBOMED index drifted down 0.03 percent to 13,213.09 on trading of 1.4 billion pesos worth of shares..
"There was a clear speculative turn being fed by the rumor of a possible heavy investment by Banco de Santander in Bancoquia," one Bogota trader said.

Bancoquia is the country's eighth-largest bank in terms of assets and the financial arm of the business empire of Julio Mario Santo Domingo, one of Colombia's leading entrepreneurs. The bank declined to comment on the speculation.
The stock climbed 9.6 percent in Bogota on volume of 46.9 million pesos and 9.6 percent in Medellin on trading of 38.2 milion pesos worth of shares.
Among other banks traded in Bogota, Banco Ganadero's ordinary shares edged up 0.8 percent to 250 each, while Banco de Bogota gained 1.65 percent, ending at 5,800.
Volume in Bogota was boosted by a 1.8 billion peso cross-trade in Parque Industrial La Candelaria and another cross-trade worth 7.7 billion pesos in Centro Internacional de Cartagena.
Both companies are involved in developing a tax-free zone in the Caribbean port city of Cartagena and are rarely traded in the markets.

Trading in Medellin was dominated by a cross-trade in chocolate manufacturer Compaa Nacional de Chocolates, part of the powerful Sindicato Antioqueo industrial conglomerate. Its share price ended unhanged at 8,300. Banco de Colombia ended down 3.0 percent to 405.01.
